messages.subject: Re: Linked brush question
messages.body_plain:
> Can you provide a bit more detail about what you trying
to do with the brush?

In bioinformatics there is the so called MA plot. You measure the activity of a few thousand genes under two different conditions and plot baseline abundance vs. fold change (typically both on log scale) (http://puriney.github.io/visay/2013/07/04/ma-plot-and-volcano-plot). Each dot represents a single gene. In an interactive version I'd like to identify the gene behind a dot using a tool tip or right button menu. Searching for a single gene of interest might also be useful.

The brush comes into place when there are more than two conditions. Say you have e.g. tested a certain cell type under two conditions, and now try the same conditions on a different cell type. The genes would be the same, but with more or less different abuandance and fold change values. Which (groups of) genes behave the same, which show up in a completely different spot in a plot of the second experiment? So I'd put the second experiment in a second plot and link them via the brush.

In real live of course there are not only two experiments, so you would need  to select the experiment on the fly from a larger data set. In todays ggvis I think I can work out almost everthing needed, but the problem of using a dynamic data set with the brush. In my test app
(https://github.com/ThomasSiegmund/ggvis-hflights/tree/brush) I've substituted the genes with flight numbers from hfligths. There is a reactive function which delivers the data to the plots as monthly subsets. But I have no idea how to use the brush with it. It seems to accept only a static data set. I've tried to make the number of rows in the data fixed and initialized the brush accordingly but this also did not work.

Thanks for your interest.

Thomas

messages.body_plain:
Hi Winston,

I have another use case for you. We are working on a (we think) neat shiny app - we'll be happy to show it off when it's done.

Part of the app involves a ggvis with two layers: (1) a background image, (2) a grid of rectangles on which a user clicks to choose a rectangle.

We would like to use scaled properties to display the image, i.e. x, x2, y, y2, so that we can translate between the image coordinates and the rectangle coordinates. It may be a further challenge to set the aspect ratio of the grid so as not to distort the image (any advice here?).

We have tried to translate the image into greyscale values, then to display as rectangles, but this was a bit slow and heavy.

In short, can the x2 and y2 properties for layer_image() be activated?

Code below.

Thanks as always,

Ian

img_size <- c(142, 60)
img_url <- "http://www.schneider-electric.com/navigation/images/se_logo.gif"

fn_grid <- function(img_size, nx, ny){

  dx <- img_size[1] / nx
  dy <- img_size[2] / ny

  x = dx * seq(0, nx - 1)
  y = dy * seq(0, ny - 1)

  x_rep <- rep(x, times = ny)
  y_rep <- rep(y, each = ny)

  df <- data.frame(
    x_min = x_rep,
    y_min = y_rep,
    x_max = x_rep + dx,
    y_max = y_rep + dy
  )

}

df_grid <- fn_grid(img_size, 2, 2)
df_img <- fn_grid(img_size, 1, 1)

# this works
df_img %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x_min, y = ~y_max, x2 = ~x_max, y2 = ~y_min) %>%
  layer_rects(fillOpacity := 0.5) %>%
  layer_rects(stroke := "red", fillOpacity := 0, data = df_grid)

# would like this to work similarly
df_img %>%
  ggvis(x = ~x_min, y = ~y_max, x2 = ~x_max, y2 = ~y_min) %>%
  layer_images(
    url := "http://www.schneider-electric.com/navigation/images/se_logo.gif"
  ) %>%
  layer_rects(stroke := "red", fillOpacity := 0, data = df_grid)

messages.body_plain:
I have a shiny app with a checkbox.  When the checkbox is unselected it will display only one population (pop1), when the checkbox is selected it will show both populations (pop1 and pop2) and fill them with a different color.  The problem is with set_options(duration = 0): if this option is not included by triggering the checkbox a few times the histograms will quite often fail to render properly.  If this option is included then the histograms will display properly but without the snazzy transitions.

Example code:

#server.R
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

set.seed(1)
pop1 = data.frame(x = rnorm(1000, 0, 1), g = rep(1, 1000))
pop2 = data.frame(x = rnorm(1000, 5, 1), g = rep(2, 1000))
data = rbind(pop1, pop2)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  choose_data = reactive({
    if(input$show) return(data %>% group_by(g))
    else return(subset(data, g == 1) %>% group_by(g))
  })

  choose_data %>% ggvis(x = ~x) %>% layer_histograms(fill = ~g) %>%
    #set_options(duration = 0) %>%  #if this is commented out strange things happen
    bind_shiny("ggvis")
})

#ui.R
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

shinyUI( fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(
        width = 2,
        checkboxInput("show", "show")
      ),

    column(
      width = 5,
      ggvisOutput("ggvis")
    )
  )
))

For example, to get the [near] equivalent of

my.df %>% group_by(my.factor) %>% arrange(my.x) %>% ggvis(x= ~my.x, y = ~my.y.min, y2 = ~my.y.max, fill = ~my.factor, alpha := .15) %>% layer_ribbons()

Except of course the alpha part doesn't work at all so if the regions overlap the ggvis output is more confusing than what I get from ggplot.

And without the post-group arrange by x I get gobbledygook.

messages.subject: On ggvis' usefulness (or lack thereof) and how it could be improved
messages.subject_clean: On ggvis' usefulness (or lack thereof) and how it could be improved
messages.body_plain:
Alas after a quick evaluation yesterday, I have a few critical comments to make about ggvis in an interactive environment. Insofar what you guys have is more or less a web clone of ggplot2, which isn't all that useful in the web world of 2014. To be useful in a interactive environment for exploratory analysis you need at least:

1) Good auto-generated tooltips [for highlighting etc.], which means x,y values and every factor that's in the vis ["layer"] by default. Sure, add a programmatic way [hooks] to change/tweak them, but don't make me program the tooltips ever time.

2) An easy, interactive way to add/remove levels of a factor to a visualization. At least an auto-generated radio buttons list, possibly add multiple range selection for continuous ones [on heat maps] etc. You have a interval widget that one could use for a single interval, but for multiple continuous intervals, I'm not even sure how to do it [using your widget set] without overloading the UI.

Note that even Excel's pivot chart can do add/remove of factor levels with a click [since the 2010 version has added "slicers"]. Moving factors between axes with drag-and-drop [which Excel also does] isn't that important in practice IMO, but it's sometimes handy. Being able map to factor to colors or shapes is more important in my book, but the brains of Microsoft apparently don't grok that, so Excel only does some useless theming with the colors in most pivot chart types because it still lacks a sufficiently general notion of binding data to an visual element in the graph, unlike stuff based on Gramar of Graphics.

And if you don't want to take the word of an anonymous dog on the Internet (I can't remove the virtual paper bag from my virtual head for good reasons), look at recommendations for interactivity on p. 27 in Tableau Software's guidebook http://mkt.tableausoftware.com/files/VisualGuidebookTabRead.pdf. They mention the first two points at least.

3) And the final ingredient for a good interactive visualization is a good animation when you do certain kinds of filtering changes. This is really important when a data set is bigger than 100 displayed points or so. Human vision is sensitive to motion but can't diff easily in the brain instant changes (aka the famous "change blindness"). Motion charts are based on this idea for time series, but you can use it for non-time data to explore "what if" and filter scenarios in almost any kind of data. I've done filterable Sunburst charts for example which were well received. (Alas I can't share the code because my employer doesn't see any benefit in that.)

Alas your chosen interposer/middleware, Vega, doesn't seem to even have a clue what animation is, even though D3 itself underneath isn't that clueless. Perhaps that happens because the theoretical model of Grammar of Graphics doesn't include any notion of interaction [like tooltips] or animation; I guess an extension in that direction would be a fairly good research topic.

I can't close this topic without mentioning that poor animation performance is still a big issue in the web world. So choose your poison wisely in this regard... I for one prefer[ed] to use JIT (JavaScript InfoVist Toolkit) over D3 for anything involving animation because of the performance issue. I can write a big brain dump about the finer points of [charts/visualization] animation with web technologies, but I'm not sure anyone on this list would want to read it... given the complete lack of such support in ggvis. In 2014 however, I'm very weary of choosing any sort of interposer/middleware that can't output WebGL directly [after IE11 adopted it in surprise move], although any middleware you chose should have a fallback backend renderer [canvas/SVG] for older/crappy browsers, of course. I'd like to see an R charting package that does 3D directly via WebGL, which would also give awesome 2D [animation] performance. The guy that wrote JIT [for 2D] later wrote PhiloGL [for 3D], which you can see in action in demos like http://www.senchalabs.org/philogl/PhiloGL/examples/worldFlights/, although I have not yet used PhiloGL myself for any project yet. There's an attempt to marry D3 with WebGL known as PathGL, but it doesn't look well done, e.g. http://pathgl.com/examples/map.html is a rather poor demo.

Ian
